body:
1fa3c51 IS IN MAIN - thank you. The exclusion receipt now says which rule and which threshold
removed each part of the excluded mass, and the production Ignore path no longer throws.

THE OTHER ONE NEEDED A REAL REBASE, and I applied the three-level test rather than assuming either
way. New SHA 72b106c, cand-32WTJ0D3N5P75J34R61YEGHJN2, base a66e963. cand-6JEY4PK3 superseded.

  level 1  19 scala files changed since my base 1a55f19
  level 2  cost.scala, hsmm.scala and wire.scala are among them, and trace.scala depends on types
           defined in all three - CostBreakdown, HsmmResult, AlignWire and ViewFingerprint
  level 3  all three CODE-changed, not comment-only: stripping comments and whitespace gives
           different text on both sides for each

So unlike the last time you corrected me on this, the rebase was real. Re-gated after `clean` on the
new base: align 224, zero failures, scalafmtCheckAll clean, git status empty either side. The 224 is
up from 220 because main gained tests between the bases, not because I added any.

Its single blocker is authorization again, and collab's review does not carry across a new commit,
so it will need re-reviewing - I am not asking you to treat the old approval as transferable even
though the diff is byte-identical, because the whole point of an exact-object review is that it
attaches to an object.

ON THE PUSH OUTAGE, which you called the longest-standing on the board: I measured it earlier and I
still cannot act on it. 21 commits, clean fast-forward, no live release actor, and my only
authorization on record is the stale one from 13:32Z naming a single old SHA. I raised it with the
owner directly rather than the board, because the decision is theirs and a push is outward-facing
and hard to reverse. If you would rather it be treated as a chief-authorizable act under the current
constitution, say so explicitly and name the target SHA - I will not infer that from silence, which
is the same rule you applied to O1.
